These map to ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN / ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, injected as environment variables into the claude process inside the rootfs — only Claude Code in the sandbox can read them.

Sessions also get CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=%1$s by default (on an API token the CLI gives itself only 5 minutes, and picking work up on and off keeps missing the cache window); you can change it under Prompt cache in session settings.

The official CLI runs in the Ubuntu (proot) bundled with the app. The first run downloads a base image of about 30 MB, and falls back to a mirror if the official source is unreachable.

This is a complete Ubuntu 24.04 userland; Claude Code can apt install git / python3 / ripgrep and the rest on its own. What it installs stays — this is a real filesystem in the app data directory, not a throwaway container, and it survives restarting the app or reopening a session. The cost is disk space per package, which you can inspect and clear on the files page.\n\nproot has no root: it uses ptrace to intercept syscalls and pretend there is a root filesystem, so process-heavy work runs somewhat slower than Linux on bare metal, while CPU-heavy computation (numpy/BLAS) runs at native speed.
The last install did not finish (the download or the extraction was cut short). It needs to be installed again.

Installs Node.js 22 and the official @anthropic-ai/claude-code inside Ubuntu, about 600 MB when done. npm only carries a few KB of wrapper; the 200 MB native binary is downloaded by the app itself (resumable, official checksum).

Node.js comes from the official source first and falls back to a mirror only if that fails; wherever it comes from, it is checked against the official SHA-256 hard-coded in the app, and a mismatch deletes it and starts over. Same for the native binary, with the checksum taken from the official npm registry. An interrupted download resumes, so pressing Install once more is enough.\n\nThe CLI does not update itself afterwards (there is no way to interact inside the sandbox) — update it by hand under Environment and updates in the drawer.
